fresh_source_check.result:
## A008: semisimplicity and scalar commutant

Consumer: lines 694-710. Sources: Faltings 1983, section 5, Satz 3 and Satz 4, printed p. 360, and the 1984 erratum, printed p. 381. Both page images were checked. Satz 3 asserts semisimplicity of the rational Tate representation over a number field. Satz 4 identifies the integral endomorphism ring tensored with Z_l with Tate-module endomorphisms; its rational consequence is the one used here. The erratum replaces the constant-height assertion in Satz 2 by eventual stationarity and explicitly says that this suffices for the later results. It does not withdraw Satz 3 or Satz 4.

Here A is over the number field L', and every geometric endomorphism is already defined over L, hence over L'. The non-CM branch assumes End^0(A_bar)=B. Thus End_G(V_l(A))=B tensor Q_l. Scalar extension commutes with this commutant: it is the simultaneous kernel of linear commutator maps, and a finite subfamily already cuts out that kernel. The finite-dimensional algebra generated by the Galois image acts semisimply. In characteristic zero its semisimple quotient is separable, so semisimplicity persists under coefficient extension, including an algebraic closure.

After splitting B, write V=r plus r. Its Galois commutant is M_2(End_G(r)), whereas Faltings gives M_2(E). Consequently End_G(r)=E, and after further scalar extension the same argument gives the scalars. A reducible semisimple module would have a nontrivial projection in its commutant. Hence r restricted to G_L' is absolutely irreducible, and so is r on the larger group. This uses semisimplicity as well as the scalar commutant; there is no claim about residual irreducibility.

Accept conditional on A007/A061/A062 and the established non-CM endomorphism algebra. No new bound or field extension is required.

full_consumer_anchor.excerpt:
\paragraph{Modularity and a uniform conductor bound.}
Choose one number field $C$ containing all $a_\sigma$, the values of
$\beta$, and a splitting field of $B$. For each coefficient prime
$\ell$ choose an embedding of $C$ into $\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell$
and extend scalars on $V_\ell(A)$ to a finite extension containing
its image. With the constant-coefficient convention above, define
\[
 \rho_\ell(\sigma)
   =\beta(\sigma)^{-1}a_\sigma\mu_\sigma\circ\sigma.
\]
The cocycle identities make this a representation of $G_\Q$.
It commutes with $B$, so matrix units give
$\rho_\ell\simeq r_\ell\oplus r_\ell$ with $\dim r_\ell=2$.
On $G_{L'}$ it is the actual Tate action of $A$.
Faltings' semisimplicity and endomorphism theorems
\cite{faltings1983} show that $r_\ell|_{G_{L'}}$ is absolutely
irreducible: after splitting $B$, its commutant is the scalars.

## A010: de Rham implies potentially semistable

Consumer: lines 711-717. Exact checked source: Berger's pinned author article `article02.pdf`, Theorem 0.7 on author p. 6 and Corollary 5.22 on author p. 52. The latter follows from the equivalence with quasi-unipotence of the differential equation and the monodromy result used there. The statement is that every de Rham p-adic representation is potentially semistable. The separate arXiv v3 has different numbering and is not silently substituted.

The input is a continuous finite-dimensional representation of G_Q5 over a finite extension E of Q5. Regard it first as a Q5 representation. A009 gives its de Rham property, not merely its Hodge-Tate weights. Berger gives a finite extension of Q5 on which it is semistable. The commuting E-action acts on the semistable comparison spaces, so the same conclusion holds with E coefficients. There is no Tate twist or sign conversion at this step. Pan needs existence of this extension; no bound on it is used in A012's separate prime-to-p torsion argument.

Accept conditional on A009 and the continuous finite-coefficient construction. Preserve the exact author-version locator in the audit.

Duality gives the H1 constituent and preserves conductor.

fresh_source_check.result: The Eisenstein derivative gives delta<=e-1+e*v_p(e). Its product over inertia conjugates gives the lower-group different sum. Herbrand change of variables yields delta/e=1-1/e+integral(1-1/|G^u|)du, bounding the last positive break by 2delta/e<=4a^2. The subgroup upper-numbering relation uses the quotient Herbrand function, whose inverse is >=identity. Semistable wild inertia is trivial away from ell; the splitting character is wild-trivial at odd p, and the p=2 fourth-power/unit-log bound is <=3e. Integrating codimension at most two yields the stated conductor bound without a further degree factor.

full_consumer_anchor.excerpt:
At $p$, take $F=L_v$ and adjoin $A[3]$, using $A[5]$ if
$p=3$. This extension has degree at most $DG_0$ over $\Q_p$.
Raynaud's criterion \cite[Theorem 3.5]{silverbergzarhin}
gives semistable reduction there. Its wild inertia acts
trivially on each $V_\ell(A)$ with $\ell\ne p$.
The preceding break bound and the subgroup rule for upper
numbering therefore show that all absolute ramification
groups above $U_0=4(DG_0)^2$ act trivially on that Tate module.
On these groups $a_\sigma\mu_\sigma=1$ because they lie in $G_L$.
For odd $p$, the character $\beta|_{G_F}$ is trivial on wild
inertia: its square is the tame character $\chi|_{G_F}$, and a
pro-$p$ group has no quotient of order two. At $p=2$, local
reciprocity and the norm map give $\beta^4=1$ on the units of
$F$, since the $2$-primary local factor of $\chi$ has conductor
at most four. If $e=v_F(2)\le D$, the local logarithm gives
$(U_F^{e+1})^4=U_F^{3e+1}$. Thus the relative upper break of
$\beta$ is at most $3e$. To make the change of numbering explicit,
the same normal-closure estimate bounds the last upper break of
$F/\mathbb Q_2$ by $4D^2$. Above it, the absolute upper group
$G_{\mathbb Q_2}^{u}$ lies in $G_F$, and the subgroup formula is
\[
 G_{\mathbb Q_2}^{u}\cap G_F
       =G_F^{\psi_{F/\mathbb Q_2}(u)},
 \qquad \psi_{F/\mathbb Q_2}(u)\ge u\quad(u\ge0).
\]
Consequently $\beta$ is trivial on every absolute upper group with
$u>\max(4D^2,3e)$, which is at most $U_0$.
This proves the asserted absolute bound without a factor involving
$[L':\mathbb Q]$.
The Artin conductor exponent of $r_\ell$ is consequently
at most $2+2U_0\le E_0$.

## A014: height of the modular Jacobian

Consumer: lines 831-840. Exact source: Javanpeykar's published ANT 8 (2014) article, Theorem 1.1.1, printed p. 90; the modular-curve discussion on pp. 92-93; section 2.1 on p. 93; section 2.3 on pp. 97-98. The theorem covers smooth projective connected curves over the algebraic closure of Q of genus at least one and gives h_Fal(X)<=13*10^6*g*deg_B(X)^5. Section 2.1 fixes the differential metric (i/2) integral omega wedge conjugate(eta). Section 2.3 identifies its curve height with the stable Faltings height of the Jacobian. These are the manuscript's original stable-height convention, with no additive normalization correction.

X_1(N) is the smooth projective connected modular curve over Q. Its map to X(1), followed by j/1728, is branched only at 0,1,infinity. Its degree is at most [SL_2(Z):Gamma_1(N)]<=N^2; passing to the effective projective action only decreases the degree. Riemann-Hurwitz for a three-point degree-d cover gives 2g-2<=d-3 and therefore g<=d. A063 gives g>=2, so the source's genus premise holds even at potentially small levels. Hence h_F(J)<=13*10^6*N^12. The premises N<=QM^2, Q>=10^12, M>=1 give h_F(J)<=Q^13*M^24 and g<=Q^3*M^4 exactly as displayed.

Accept conditional on A011's modular realization, the established level bound, and A063. The theorem does not itself extract A as an isogeny factor.

## A015: bounded isogeny in the required direction

Consumer: lines 842-857. Exact source: the pinned published Duke 163 (2014) article by Gaudron-Remond, printed p. 2058 for kappa(A) and the original stable-height convention; Theorem 1.4 on p. 2060; the definition of a couple of isogenies on p. 2059. Original page images confirm alpha(g)=2^10*g^3 and the inner exponent 64*g^2. The theorem supplies isogenies in both directions between k-defined abelian varieties which are K-isogenous, of degree at most kappa(A). It does not require principal polarizations.

Take k=K=L', source J, and target A times Z. A063 supplies the isogeny over L'. Although that construction first gives A times Z -> J, the theorem supplies J -> A times Z using the source height h_F(J). Taking logarithms of kappa(J) gives precisely the three terms in lines 846-848.

For T=QM^4, the logarithms log(14g), log d', and log max(h_F(J),log d',1) are at most 5T, 2T, and 19T. For the last term, the maximum itself is at most Q^13*M^24, including the possibly negative height. These follow from log Q<=Q, log M<=M^4/4, and Q>=10^12. The parenthesis is at most 320Q^7*M^12+40QM^4<=360Q^7*M^12. Multiplication by 1024g^3<=1024Q^9*M^12 gives 368640Q^16*M^24<=Q^17*M^24. Both the dimension powers and the exponent 24 are preserved.

Accept conditional on A014/A063 and the preceding bounds for N and [L':Q]. The separate CM use of the same published theorem at lines 591-596 belongs to A005, not A015; it is not silently accepted by this disposition.

## A016: lower bound for the complementary factor

Consumer: lines 858-864. Exact source: Gaudron-Remond section 9, printed p. 2098, in the proof of Lemma 9.1, explicitly using h_F(C)>=-(3/2)dim C and warning about the difference between height normalizations. The same general lower bound is used again on p. 2101. The manuscript uses the original stable h_F, so this is the correct bound.

For dim Z=g-2, it implies h_F(Z)>=-2g. If Z has dimension zero, its determinant line is trivial and its height is zero, giving the same inequality without an application of a positive-dimensional theorem. Additivity and isogeny variation from A006 then give the bound at line 862. The last absorption is Q^-4+2Q^-14*M^-20<=1/2, valid for Q>=10^12, M>=1. No assertion h_F(Z)>=0 is needed.

fresh_source_check.result:
## A016: lower bound for the complementary factor

Consumer: lines 858-864. Exact source: Gaudron-Remond section 9, printed p. 2098, in the proof of Lemma 9.1, explicitly using h_F(C)>=-(3/2)dim C and warning about the difference between height normalizations. The same general lower bound is used again on p. 2101. The manuscript uses the original stable h_F, so this is the correct bound.

For dim Z=g-2, it implies h_F(Z)>=-2g. If Z has dimension zero, its determinant line is trivial and its height is zero, giving the same inequality without an application of a positive-dimensional theorem. Additivity and isogeny variation from A006 then give the bound at line 862. The last absorption is Q^-4+2Q^-14*M^-20<=1/2, valid for Q>=10^12, M>=1. No assertion h_F(Z)>=0 is needed.

Accept conditional on A006, A014, A015 and A063. The Bost bound is accepted as the exact published input stated and used by Gaudron-Remond; this is not a claim to have re-proved Bost's theorem.

Consumers: L2374–2388 and L8882–9052, including all eight recorded citation sites. Primary locators: Cornut–Jetchev H.1–H.3 and sections 3.1–3.3, pp.4–6; Lemma 2.1, p.4; Theorem 3.1 and Corollary 3.2, p.9; section 3.6 and Lemma 3.4, pp.9–10; sections 4.9–4.10, pp.15–16. The newly recorded global embedding prerequisite belongs to A052 below.

The substitution is base field Q, imaginary quadratic field F=Q(sqrt(Dh_*)), source algebra M2(Q), and changed set {ell_0}. The set avoids finite source ramification, its parity is 1+0+1=2, and its single place is inert since the support imposes (D/ell_0)=1 and (h_*/ell_0)=−1. It avoids N and the quadratic discriminant. Both fine conductors are one: intersecting with either containing maximal order cannot enlarge the maximal quadratic order. The local distance at ell_0 is zero, so Lemma 2.1(ii) gives N_ell(0,0,0)=1, and the relative class-field factor is one. Thus the source's kappa is exactly one.

The source target is the specified sign fiber, not both residue orientations. At the old split prime powers Lemma 2.1(iv) gives two choices even when the prime is 2; in the division algebra the norm valuation modulo two gives the separate two residue orientations. The target count is therefore 2^(omega(N)+1). The manuscript retains these orientations. Its embedding stabilizer is O_F^times={±1}, so the factor from counting actual vectors and dividing by the automorphism group is 1/2. Combining these gives exactly 2^omega(N), with no further quotient by conjugate pairs. Section 4 identifies the equivariant adelic map with reduction of the same enhanced elliptic curve. Consequently the genus-weighted unaveraged sum is the same P_D, not an averaged or different-conductor point. Inverting Artin symbols reindexes the sum harmlessly because its character is quadratic.

The arithmetic/geometric Frobenius ambiguity disappears on the indicated F_(ell_0^2) points. Outside the inert support the consumer asserts zero, not the reduction formula. ## A029 — full-space Fourier proportionality

Consumers: L2405–2419 and L7633–7731. Primary locators: Waldspurger 1981 section I.2, Proposition 2, p.377; Corollary 2 and its proof, pp.483–484. The source defines the full almost-all-Hecke space and states its coefficient identity for every member. Its proof explicitly extends the linear identity by linearity before squaring.

Use k=3, chi=psi, chi_0=psi chi_(−1), phi_0=f_E tensor eta, eta=psi chi_(−sigma), n1=D0 and n2=D. Then phi_0 tensor chi_0^−1=f_E tensor chi_sigma. Nonzero existence has already been supplied by A030, so Proposition 2 supplies H1 rather than the manuscript assuming H1 for an arbitrary packet. The ratio D/D0 is a square at every prime in the actual level support S0, including 2. The final paragraph of p.484 explicitly removes H2 in this same-dyadic-squareclass comparison.

The printed character is chi(n2/n1), hence psi(D/D0). The printed exponent is k/2−1=1/2, giving the displayed square-root normalization. The corollary concerns literal squares, not absolute-value squares. A nonzero reference coefficient and central value permit the stated division. Polarization over characteristic zero gives one proportionality scalar for the entire space; zero analytic value gives the zero functional. Old multiplicities are retained. The later common-level comparison has only S0 prime support; the extra coprimality sieve is applied afterwards. No dimension-one assumption or missing good-prime factor is used.

Consumers: L7513–7632. Primary locators: Waldspurger ICM, Proposition 1 p.527 and Theorem 1 p.529; 1981 Proposition 18 proof pp.466–467 and section I.3 pp.377–378.

The ICM theorem gives nonzero lift from the nonzero central value; Proposition 1 places a nonzero lift in the indicated irreducible cuspidal space. The 1981 proof connects this nonzero value with the nonzero specified Fourier functional. The packet is chosen by this lift and frequency, not chosen arbitrarily first. Positive real frequency selects the holomorphic weight-3/2 constituent. The elementary unary constituents are outside this cuspidal packet scope.

## A031 — algebraic section model and descent

Consumers: L7733–7810. Primary locators: Ramsey Definition 3.1, printed p.606/PDF p.9; Theorem 4.2, p.609/PDF p.12; Remark 4.4, p.610/PDF p.13.

Definition 3.1 applies to k=3 and any positive auxiliary N over a ring in which 4N is invertible. The consumer works over characteristic-zero fields and includes character values and cusp roots of unity in one number field. Theorem 4.2 is a q-expansion descent statement in its stated module convention, not a general cohomology-vanishing theorem. The consumer's finite-affine-cover kernel argument proves the only base change used: flat extension between fields. Finite dimensionality reduces its algebraic linear constraints to finitely many equations. Nonzero reference evaluation therefore descends to an algebraic vector and can be normalized to one. Remark 4.4's warning about weights 1/2 and 3/2 is respected.

The Galois comparison is a separate manuscript argument: coefficient conjugation transports psi to psi^e, while twisting by nu=eta^((e−1)/2) supplies the same character and good eigenvalues. Both operations remain at S0-supported level; D0 is prime to it. A029 then compares their normalized coefficient functionals. Nothing in Ramsey alone is represented as proving rational coefficient ratios or preserving an unchanged character under Galois action.

Consumers: L7733–7810. Primary locators: Ramsey Definition 3.1, printed p.606/PDF p.9; Theorem 4.2, p.609/PDF p.12; Remark 4.4, p.610/PDF p.13.

Definition 3.1 applies to k=3 and any positive auxiliary N over a ring in which 4N is invertible. The consumer works over characteristic-zero fields and includes character values and cusp roots of unity in one number field. Theorem 4.2 is a q-expansion descent statement in its stated module convention, not a general cohomology-vanishing theorem. The consumer's finite-affine-cover kernel argument proves the only base change used: flat extension between fields. Finite dimensionality reduces its algebraic linear constraints to finitely many equations. Nonzero reference evaluation therefore descends to an algebraic vector and can be normalized to one. Remark 4.4's warning about weights 1/2 and 3/2 is respected.

The Galois comparison is a separate manuscript argument: coefficient conjugation transports psi to psi^e, while twisting by nu=eta^((e−1)/2) supplies the same character and good eigenvalues. Both operations remain at S0-supported level; D0 is prime to it. A029 then compares their normalized coefficient functionals. Nothing in Ramsey alone is represented as proving rational coefficient ratios or preserving an unchanged character under Galois action.

## A033 — non-CM open image

Consumers: L2733–2763, L3349–3385 and L8010–8032. Primary locator: Serre 1972 opening theorem and reformulation, pp.259–260. The actual j=35152/9 is a nonintegral rational number, so this elliptic curve and its quadratic twists are non-CM. Serre's theorem applies over Q and includes the 2-adic component. It requires neither rational 2-torsion to be absent nor residual surjectivity.

Openness supplies 1+2^n M2(Z2) and a nontrivial central scalar. The first consumer then constructs g² tau g² tau^−1, using generalized-dihedral ring-class action to fix each field; its image is u^4 I and v2(u^4−1)=n+2. Squaring the displayed matrix preimages places them in any quadratic kernel, and their Z2-span contains 2^(n+1)M2(Z2). The second consumer restricts to determinant one, intersects an index-at-most-two subgroup, and uses explicit unipotent/commutator products to obtain its congruence subgroup inside the actual radical-fixing kernel. It does not invoke linear disjointness. The third uses irreducibility and the central scalar to prove the Kummer image spans the rational Tate module; compactness and finite index then give the integral lattices stated there. These are manuscript deductions from openness, not stronger assertions attributed to Serre. No parameter-uniform theorem about all auxiliary Kummer extensions is silently imported.

## A034 — Heegner norm relations

Consumer: L2765–2789. Primary locator: Cai–Chen–Liu, Theorem 2.15, printed p.3730/PDF p.10, with condition (*) on p.3722.

Take source base conductor c=d and old multiplier m=1 for each currently used d. All N-primes split, so N1=1, X_K(N)=X0(N), and (*) reduces to (d,N)=1. The new prime avoids 6dND_K. This application does not require d itself to be an inert squarefree product. The source's u1 is [O_K^times:Z^times]=1; the field exclusions ensure exactly this. Its inert trace is T_ell and its split trace is T_q minus the two Frobenius actions. The product of the latter Artin symbols is the principal ideal (q), so they are inverses. Passing to the fixed elliptic quotient gives the displayed eigenvalues. The cusp at infinity removes the degree correction; any previously chosen cusp translation is killed by the fixed C_pi. The source sum is unaveraged. No class-number or conductor-dependent multiplier is introduced.

## A035 — Frobenius congruence, restricted source role

Consumer: L2791–2810. Primary locator: Howard arXiv:1202.6340v1, section 1.7, formula (13), printed/PDF p.19.

Howard's formula has the displayed arithmetic Frobenius at a compatible place and his restricted n-family. The manuscript accurately labels it as a record of that special case, not a theorem for arbitrary d. Its broader assertion is proved locally: d prime to ell makes the CM order maximal unramified quadratic at ell; inert reduction is supersingular; the raising isogenies specialize to the unique subgroup scheme of order ell, the relative Frobenius kernel. The prime-to-ell cyclic N-structure follows the same map. Good integral models extend the fixed quotient. Transporting the place with the old class action gives the equivariance needed. No odd coefficient-prime or residual-surjectivity hypothesis from Howard's unrelated Kolyvagin theorem is imported. Accept as a corroborating source with the supplied broader local argument, not as a direct arbitrary-conductor application of (13).

verbatim_application_proposal.hypothesis_status: The connected smooth special fiber is a connected commutative algebraic group over the finite residue field, even at bad reduction. Lang surjectivity kills its finite-field H1; inflation-restriction injects the finite residue-extension H1 into that group. Smooth reduction is surjective. For the kernel, the extension is unramified, a base uniformizer is Galois fixed, and each formal filtration quotient is the additive residue extension, induced by a normal basis. Successively corrected coboundaries converge in the complete formal group; finiteness of Gal allows simultaneous limits in every cocycle equation. Finally B(Fprime)/B0(Fprime) embeds into the geometric component group, so its order c_B kills its H1 and hence H1(Gal,B(Fprime)). ## A052 — quaternionic geometry, including new coverage obligations

Consumers: L8153–8180 and L8839–8843. Primary locators: Jetchev–Kane v1 sections 1.1–1.2, pp.1–2, and 2.5, p.6; Voight corrected online v1.0.7u (August 5, 2026), Main Theorem 14.6.1 p.223/PDF p.243 and Proposition 14.6.7 p.224/PDF p.244. Voight SHA256 is `a9316b834dbd500c52cd3a981c3205c9f4145b217042b213d23f696aee84b0f0`.

Jetchev–Kane takes general N>1 with ell prime to N, not squarefree N. Its enhanced supersingular curves have Eichler endomorphism orders of full level N, automorphisms R_z^times, and the stated adelic double-coset description. Its field-of-definition statement and the scalar-Frobenius explanation in the consumer handle prime-power cyclic subgroups. We do not use its later orbit-count corollary or identify its unweighted ternary lattice with the present weighted Schwartz construction. That distinction leaves the weighted modularity in A053/A054 and exact orientation count in A028.

Voight's classification applies over Q to the two noncomplex places {ell_0,infinity}. His embedding proposition applies to the separable quadratic extension Q(sqrt(Dh_*)): the real completion is C, and the ell_0 completion is a field by inertness. These are all the ramified places. Thus a rational embedding exists. This is not an optimal embedding into an arbitrarily fixed global order. The following choice of z0 is adelically variable and uses the preceding local constructions; no selectivity assertion is being assumed.

## A053 — local Weil operators

Consumers: L8312–8563. Primary locators: Weil 1964 I.13–I.14/Theorem 2, pp.160–162; II.25, p.173; II.28/Proposition 4, pp.175–177.

The local field is Q_p (including 2) or R, the nondegenerate form has rank three, the additive character is fixed globally, and the self-dual measure is |det(2A)|_v^(1/2) times coordinate measure. The Fourier pairing is B_Q=2x^tAy. These yield Fourier-square reflection and the stated completed-square integral. Compact translation invariance of the actual locally constant weights supplies dual-lattice support and lower-unipotent invariance. No self-duality of Z2^3 is incorrectly assumed: its reference dual is (1/2)Z2^3 with measure 2^(−3/2).

The index identity follows from the quaternion norm form <1,−u,−a,ua>, multiplicativity and the split/division values +1/−1. The determinant quotient relative to Q0 is therefore (u,det Q), including at 2. The manuscript uses the same Fourier convention and lifts for both rank-three representations. Changing both conventions inverses the indices without changing this quadratic quotient. Its explicit common-cover relations retain the order-four lift of −I at 2. For Q_B the determinant is square; for Q_B/m its squareclass is m. Thus there is no missing dyadic squareclass 2 or uncontrolled eighth-root factor. This checks the convention-sensitive external interface; the finite local weight recipes are internal constructions, not an extra conclusion of Weil's theorem.

## A054 — global theta modularity and cusp holomorphy

Consumers: L8627–8725. Primary locators: Weil II.27, pp.174–175; II.30/Proposition 5, p.179; III.41/Theorem 6, p.193.

Outside the prescribed finite support, the characteristic function is that of an integral self-dual lattice at an odd split place, so the local index and spherical action are trivial. At the remaining places A053 supplies the required congruence invariance. The finite tensor times the real Gaussian is a Schwartz–Bruhat function. Proposition 5 gives the product of local indices equal to one; the product formula also cancels the determinant measure factors. Theorem 6 therefore gives rational invariance of its theta sum. The archimedean Gaussian has weight 3/2. At an arbitrary rational cusp the finite transform still has bounded-denominator lattice-coset support; positive definiteness gives nonnegative exponents and normal convergence. This supplies holomorphy, a conclusion the source's invariance theorem alone does not state.

The adelic identity in the consumer uses gamma_f^−1, so the relative character is evaluated at its upper-left entry d. Extraction replaces Q_B by Q_B/m with the same weights; coefficients are exactly H_M(mn), with no Haar-measure multiplier in this discrete sum. Its determinant quotient produces (m/d), and division by the stated genus character gives chi_(−1). All level primes remain in the original support.

**Inventory correction required:** the existing A054 record claims an odd-factor proof of zero constant terms at every cusp. The actual baseline consumer here asserts M_(3/2), not cuspidality, and supplies only the holomorphy argument just checked. Remove the unused stronger cusp-vanishing obligation and narrow the translation to automorphy plus holomorphy at every cusp. Do not falsely record that a cusp-vanishing proof appears at these anchors. This is a record-scope correction, not a manuscript defect. The separate even-source cuspidality belongs to A030.

## A062: scalar correction and sign cocycle

Consumer: lines 608-637. Exact source: Milne CFT v4.03, Chapter IV, Theorem 2.10, the Skolem-Noether theorem. It applies to homomorphisms from a simple algebra to a central simple algebra. Set both algebras equal to B over Q, with maps identity and b -> psi_sigma sigma(b) psi_sigma^-1. The latter is a Q-algebra automorphism because all the identified endomorphisms belong to B. If this automorphism is conjugation by u, replace psi_sigma by u^-1 psi_sigma, then clear denominators. This gives a B-linear actual isogeny mu_sigma from sigma(A) to A, over L because the full relevant Hom group is defined there.

The composite mu_sigma sigma(mu_tau) mu_sigma_tau^-1 is an invertible rational endomorphism of A commuting with B. Its centralizer in End^0(A)=B is Q, so the discrepancy is c in Q^times. This centralizer is not taken inside all homology endomorphisms. Let d_sigma=deg(mu_sigma)>0. Multiplicativity gives c^4=d_sigma*d_tau/d_sigma_tau since dim A=2. With a_sigma=d_sigma^-1/4 the rescaled discrepancy has fourth power one and is real, hence is +/-1. Added coefficients carry trivial Galois action, as explicitly stated in the consumer. Associativity gives the cocycle identity. The normalized choice mu_1=1 gives the normalized cocycle. Finite choices and trivial action of G_L on the Hom groups make it inflate from Gal(L/Q).

Accept conditional on A061 and the earlier geometric isomorphisms between the conjugate fibers, and on the non-CM identity End^0(A_bar)=B. No new field or degree bound is assumed.

## A063: actual Hom and complement over L'

Consumer: lines 824-831. Exact sources: Faltings 1983, section 5, Corollary 1, printed p. 361, with the 1984 erratum discussed above; Milne AV v2.00, Part I Proposition 10.1 and its proof, printed p. 42. The latter proof constructs the complement of a specified abelian subvariety using the connected kernel of its dual inclusion composed with a polarization. It works over the ground field. The note about imperfect fields is irrelevant over L'.

A011 supplies the modular realization over a common finite coefficient field; restricting to G_L' and using the two-copy identification gives the stated common constituent of V_l(A) and V_l(J). Faltings semisimplicity means common constituent here supplies a nonzero equivariant map A-to-J on Tate spaces, after coefficient extension. Invariants in finite-dimensional Hom commute with extension: a finite intersection of kernels defines the invariant space, even when the group is infinite. Therefore there was a nonzero rational l-adic invariant before extending coefficients. Faltings' Hom isomorphism then implies Hom_L'(A,J) is nonzero. It is enough that this group tensored with Q_l is nonzero; one need not claim the specific invariant matrix is an actual integral morphism.

The non-CM quaternion division endomorphism algebra makes A absolutely simple, as in the preceding branch. A nonzero morphism A -> J has finite kernel and image B0 of dimension two. Milne's complement Z to B0 in J is defined over L', and A times Z -> J is an L'-isogeny. Its dimension gives g>=2. This is the direction initially constructed; A015 supplies the opposite direction with its bound.

Accept conditional on A008/A011 and the established non-CM quaternion endomorphism algebra. No descent of Z beyond L' or integral equality of Tate lattices is claimed.
